title: Keyboard Manager - Remapping is overriden by built in Windows Hotkeys.

judgment.rationale: The author and a commenter supplied repeatable Alt/Win remappings and concrete Windows shortcuts that still activate or fail. The report is old, so maintainer-side testing on a current supported build is needed before suggesting an engine change.
evidence: The original report remaps Left Alt to Left Win and Left Win to Left Alt, then reports Alt+G/Alt+W opening Xbox Game Bar.
A commenter reports related behavior with Right Alt/Right Win and Win+R, Win+Shift+S, and different Alt-letter combinations.
Another commenter says removing Microsoft.XboxGamingOverlay removes the overlay but does not restore the intended remapped command.
The report is cross-referenced by #40976 as a similar 'Keys double binding' report, but that issue has no linked fix.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the exact left/right modifier swaps on a current Windows build and determine whether the system shortcut or remapped target receives the event.

fix_assessment.rationale: No concrete linked implementation covers this report. The issue does not establish whether Keyboard Manager's injected modifier state or Windows' system-shortcut handling is responsible.

proposed_fixes.title: Ensure swapped Alt/Win modifiers suppress the original Windows shortcut
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the original modifier combination may still be visible to Windows' registered system-shortcut handling when Keyboard Manager injects the swapped modifier state. The report does not prove whether the hook, key-up sequence, or an external hotkey owns the behavior.
plan: Reproduce the left and right Alt/Win swap on a current build and record the exact source and target for each test.
Test the same remaps with the Xbox Game Bar overlay disabled to separate overlay display from the underlying system shortcut.
Trace the Keyboard Manager event sequence and dummy/key-up suppression for the failing chords.

If the original system chord escapes suppression, correct the event ordering and add tests for the reproduced shortcut; otherwise classify the remaining behavior as a Windows or external-handler limitation.
verification: Verify Alt+G and Alt+W produce only the configured remapped output and do not launch the Game Bar.
Verify Win+R and Win+Shift+S behave according to their configured mappings.
Repeat for right-side modifiers and confirm no modifier is left stuck.

confidence.rationale: The issue includes concrete examples, but reports vary across left/right keys and Windows shortcuts and the most recent evidence is old.

issue_context.summary: Swapping Alt and Win reportedly allows Windows shortcuts such as Game Bar to activate or causes remapped shortcuts to stop working, with differing results across modifier sides.
known_information: The original report used PowerToys 0.69.1 on an unspecified Windows build and ran PowerToys as administrator.
The original sequence swaps Left Alt and Left Win, then tests Alt+G and Alt+W.
Comments add Right Alt/Win and Win+R/Win+Shift+S examples; removing the Xbox overlay hides it but does not produce the intended command.
Related issue #40976 is open and labels this report as similar; its bot comment does not establish a fix.
inferences: The issue may involve suppression or ordering of injected modifier events, but external Windows shortcut handling remains a competing explanation.
The reported behavior may differ by modifier side or Windows feature; the examples should be retested separately.
issue_context.analysis: The public sequence is sufficient for a maintainer test. Comparing the remapped output and the system shortcut while isolating the overlay is more discriminating than asking for a broad diagnostic package.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body and all three comments, including the Xbox overlay workaround and additional modifier-side examples.
Checked the related open #40976 status; it is only a similarity cross-reference, not an implementation.
Reviewed the Keyboard Manager event-handler history and current modifier reset/suppression paths; no code evidence confirms the reported root cause.

actions.label: Reproduce Alt and Win shortcut swaps

reproduce.version_requirement: Use a current supported PowerToys build on a current supported Windows build; the report used PowerToys 0.69.1.
prerequisites: A test account where Windows shortcuts can be exercised.
Xbox Game Bar available for the Alt+G/Alt+W comparison.
steps: Remap Left Alt to Left Win and Left Win to Left Alt.
Press Alt+G and Alt+W and record whether the Game Bar opens or the configured target is sent.
Test Win+R and Win+Shift+S, then repeat with the right-side Alt/Win mappings separately.
If the Game Bar opens, temporarily disable only its overlay and repeat to distinguish the overlay from the underlying key event.
reproduce.expected: Only the configured remapped shortcut is received; the original Windows system shortcut does not fire, and no modifier remains stuck.

actions.label: Approve focused modifier investigation
actions.note: The proposed root cause remains red pending current-build reproduction.
